subject: Edge finishing and assembly quality
hook: Cutting list in, square carcass out: six stages.
ig:
Cutting list in, square carcass out: these are the six stages a trade order typically goes through in our workshop.

1. The list is checked: sizes, décor, grain, edges.
2. Panels are cut on the sliding table panel saw and labelled.
3. Edges are banded in the ABS thickness you've specified.
4. Hinge cups, shelf-pin rows and dowels are bored on the multi-spindle boring machine.
5. The carcass is assembled and checked for square.
6. Ready to collect, or delivered as agreed.

You can come in at any stage. Some fitters only want panels cut. Others want them cut, edged and drilled, then build on site. Others want carcasses assembled and ready to fit.

The images show the principle rather than a specific order. Want to know which stages would suit your next job? Use the link in bio to see our assembly service.
fb:
For trade customers wondering what happens after you send us a cutting list, here's the typical journey through our Hanley workshop.

We check the list, cut the panels on the panel saw, band the edges, drill hinge cups and shelf-pin rows on the boring machine, then assemble and check each carcass for square. After that it's ready to collect or deliver.

You don't have to take every stage. Plenty of fitters just want cutting and edging, others want ready-built carcasses.

Have a look at our assembly service and tell us what your next job needs.

on_asset: F1: Cutting list checked — Sizes, board décor, grain direction and edges marked are checked before a single panel is cut. | F2: Cut — Panels cut to size on the sliding table panel saw and labelled to match the list. | F3: Edged — Visible and working edges banded in 0.4, 1 or 2 mm ABS to match the face. | F4: Drilled — Hinge cups, shelf-pin rows and dowel holes bored on the multi-spindle boring machine. | F5: Assembled and checked — Carcass built and checked for square, because a square box is what makes doors hang true. | F6: Ready — Collected from the workshop or delivered, as agreed for the job. | Concept image
